text.content:
Security, banking, and a hand in everything else. Back in Night City, invited.

Headquarters: Tokyo. In Night City: the Waterfront, a tower going up on the Corporate Plaza ring, the Arasaka Industrial Park in Arroyo, and a family estate in North Oak
Industry: Security, banking, arms, and hundreds of subsidiaries
Leadership: Saburo Arasaka, CEO since 1960. Michiko Arasaka is the family's Accord Liaison in Night City
In Night City: Holds the Arasaka Waterfront as extraterritorial land under the Arvin Accord, and a non-voting chair at every Council session
Dealing with edgerunners: Hires through layers of deniability. Trespassers on the Waterfront are "processed"

The oldest megacorp still standing. Arasaka fought Militech in the 4th Corporate War, lost its Night City tower to a nuclear blast on 20 August 2023, and was thrown out of America for it. For twenty-four years the NUSA blamed Arasaka for the bomb; since Trace Santiago's exposé in 2047, the country has believed Militech set it off.

In June 2070 Councilman Lucius Rhyne called Tokyo, and the next morning an Arasaka supercarrier sailed into Coronado Bay and the NUSA's advance stopped. The Arvin Accord paid for it: Arasaka took the Watson waterfront and the old NorCal base behind it as sovereign land, the last empty lot on the Corporate Plaza's outer ring, and a chair at every Council session that can't vote and doesn't need to.

Arasaka in Night City, 2070

  • Arasaka Waterfront. Extraterritorial. Arasaka's main port in the Western Hemisphere, with the supercarrier at anchor offshore. Night City law stops at the gate.
  • Arasaka Tower Site. A new tower is going up on the Corporate Plaza ring where the old one fell, facing the memorial.
  • Arasaka Industrial Park. The biggest supply depot in the city, in Arroyo, growing since the Accord as Arasaka buys up idle plants.
  • The Clock Tower. Danger Gal's old headquarters in Downtown, now the Arasaka Liaison Office.
  • Arasaka Estate. A garden estate in North Oak behind three walls, kept for family visits.

The Tyger Claws were Arasaka's sword in Night City before the bomb, and their ties never fully broke. Banking and security make most of Arasaka's money, but some subsidiary of it makes, imports or sells almost anything you can name. On the NET it is buying every pre-Krash archive it can find.

Edgerunner's Handbook p.23; Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.01, 05, 08
